ev-6540220d2ce6d940.title: PostgreSQL SELECT locking clause (paraphrase)
ev-6540220d2ce6d940.text: With SKIP LOCKED, rows that cannot be locked immediately are skipped instead of waiting. The documentation says skipping locked rows gives an inconsistent view of the data, so it is not suitable for general-purpose queries, but it can be used to avoid lock contention when several consumers read from a queue-like table. FOR UPDATE locks the selected rows until the transaction ends.

ev-6999b3191ecda5ae.title: PostgreSQL explicit locking (paraphrase)
ev-6999b3191ecda5ae.text: Row-level locks acquired with FOR UPDATE are held until the transaction commits or rolls back. If the session ends abnormally, the transaction is rolled back and its locks are released, so another transaction can then lock the same rows. Locks taken by a transaction that is still open keep blocking conflicting lockers, so long transactions hold locks for their whole duration. Deadlocks are detected and one transaction is aborted with an error that the application must handle, typically by retrying the transaction.
